name: Battle of Leipzig
note: The plan shows the operation of 18 and 19 October 1813 round the city, not a single field; each block is an army, a corps group or a front. The accounts do not give exact positions, so each formation stands on the side of Leipzig that the account names. Wachau and Liebertwolkwitz are called the western flank of the French positions, but Probstheida, where the Allies advanced through them, is a village southeast of Leipzig; the south-eastern front is placed there. The Army of the North is placed to the north-east, where it crossed the Parthe. The first two days of fighting are left out.

phases.title: The French round Leipzig, the Coalition armies closing
phases.text: Napoleon drew his army round Leipzig, with Ney and Marmont on the north, MacDonald on the east, Poniatowski and Augereau on the south-east and Bertrand's corps at Lindenau. The Coalition armies stood round them.
phases.quote: He deployed his army around the city, but concentrated his force from Taucha through Stötteritz, where he placed his command.

phases.title: The Coalition attacks from all sides
phases.text: The Allies attacked from every side and completely encircled the French army. After over nine hours of fighting the French were slowly forced back towards Leipzig.
phases.quote: In over nine hours of fighting, in which both sides suffered heavy casualties, the French troops were slowly forced back towards Leipzig.

phases.title: Bertrand drives the Austrians from Lindenau
phases.text: On the western side the French IV Corps drove the Austrian III Corps away from Lindenau. This broke the encirclement and cleared the way for the French retreat.
phases.quote: This broke the encirclement which the Allied forces earlier had made against the Grande Armée, clearing the way for its retreat which would take place later the next day.

phases.title: The French withdraw in the night
phases.text: The French army was ordered to withdraw silently through Leipzig and over its single bridge across the Elster. A rearguard was left to hold the city for a day or a little longer, while the Allies did not realise that the army was leaving.
phases.quote: They were ordered to hold it for a day or a bit longer, in order to allow the rest of the army, its artillery, and its equipment sufficient time to evacuate.

phases.title: The Allies storm Leipzig
phases.text: The Allies learned of the evacuation at 7 am and attacked from the north, south and east. Oudinot's rearguard held them up in street fighting among barricades and houses.
phases.quote: they launched a full-scale assault from the north, south, and east against the retreating French.

phases.title: The bridge is blown and the rearguard is cut off
phases.text: A corporal fired the fuses of the only bridge over the Elster while it was crowded with French troops and Oudinot's rearguard was still in Leipzig. The panic became a rout in which thousands died and 30,000 were captured. The rest of the army had crossed.
phases.quote: The explosion and subsequent panic caused a rout that resulted in the deaths of thousands of French troops and the capture of 30,000 others.
